text: Most people think coding agents are about prompts. They're not. They're about your repo: the why, the map, the rules, the workflows. Get those 4 right and the agent behaves like an engineer instead of a chatbot. A thread on each 👇
THE 5-LAYER STACK FOR CODING AGENTS: memory file, skills, hooks, subagents, MCP. Master these 5 layers and you will never write code the old way again.
Moved our test command into AGENTS.md as one line: `pnpm test --run`. Before that the agent kept starting the watcher and hung for 10 minutes. Codex and Claude Code both pick it up now.

Packaged my game-modding notes into a skill folder for my coding agent: one SKILL.md for decompiling, one for swapping assets, plus two shell scripts. Works in Claude Code, still rough on Windows paths.
This AGENTS.md turns Claude Code and Codex into senior engineers. Plan first. Smallest change. Delete dead code. Run the tests. Copy it below 👇

Measured on our monorepo: a 40-line CLAUDE.md instead of the old 400-line one cut the agent's "which package?" questions from 9 to 2 across 20 tasks. Repo map at the top, commands right after.
Plugin systems for coding agents are where editors were ten years ago. One practical point for today: keep plugin hooks idempotent, because the agent may retry the same tool call.
Can't believe this 🤯 asked my agent what it wanted for its birthday and it offered to refactor my whole desktop.
Mẹo nhỏ: thêm một hook chặn agent sửa file trong thư mục `migrations/`. Từ khi có hook, agent phải hỏi trước, không còn tự sửa migration cũ. Hook dài 15 dòng, mình dán ở reply.
Paste this AGENTS.md and 3 bad agent habits disappear: hoarding old code, compat shims for an app with zero users, tests for one-line changes. Plan first, smallest change. Copy 👇

Wrote a PostToolUse hook that runs `prettier --write` only on the file the agent just edited (the path comes from the hook input JSON). Formatting the whole repo took 40 s per edit; this takes under 1 s.
Two agent tools now accept each other's plugin manifests. I tried 3 example plugins across both: 2 loaded unchanged, 1 needed a renamed config key.

If you run long subagents, put their instructions in `.claude/agents/<name>.md` instead of pasting them into the main prompt. On my refactor runs the main context stayed about 30% smaller, and each subagent gets its own tool allowlist.

Local setup numbers: one planner model plus 3 parallel subagents on a single desktop GPU. Planner about 60 tok/s, subagents about 25 tok/s each. Fine for refactors, too slow for big test generation.
